Actually, if you pay attention to the Harvard Law School symposiums on institutional corruption, that's precisely what they say about the USA. Particularly under feminism, it has replaced an old fashioned easy to see through kind of corruption with nothing other than a more sophisticated version of the exact same kind of corruption. In other words, things haven't changed. Well, no they have. Notice how if Kristof were able to pay for sexual favors with a credit card using an independent pimp, his sexual appetites might affect his journalism a bit in certain ways, but not as much as if the publisher provides sexual favors. Or is it the publisher that does? Or is it the major advertisers and businesses the NYT covers that does? For the publisher to provide reporters with sexual favors allows him to control reporters well enough so he can shake down the business world for even more money than he could, if same reporter could just go hire sex from a pimp. All in all, what you have is more centralized control. And note with increasing feminism comes increasing concentration of wealth at the top? No accident that corruption has become more sophisticated even as this has happened.
